content.text: All four subsections align with our preferred position, and no other clause creates a change-of-control right against us.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets the preferred position in full. 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate or an M&A successor (notice only). 24.2 binds Vendor asymmetrically in our favour: no assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent (reasonableness standard qualified only for capable, financially sound assignees), plus an absolute bar on assignment to a direct Customer competitor. 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control, and requires cooperation with administrative changes for a permitted successor. 24.3's mutual consent requirement is scoped to "other assignments," so it does not cut back the 24.1 carve-out, and the "void" language applies only to assignments contrary to the Section. Cross-checks are clean: 13.3 lets Customer transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with a Section 24 assignment and limits Vendor's revocation/suspension rights; 9.2's insolvency termination right is mutual and expressly excludes a lawful reorganization that does not impair performance, so it is not a back-door change-of-control exit. No "deemed an assignment" or repricing trigger appears elsewhere in the document. No redline needed.
